items.text: A theory $T\colon \mathbf{Cat}_D\to\mathbf{Cat}$, $C\mapsto T(C)$ (structures of type $T$ in $C$). $T$ is representable by $R\in\mathbf{Cat}_D$ if
T(C)\ \simeq\ \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_D(R,C)\quad(\text{natural in } C),\qquad \text{universal element in } T(R)
Morphisms of theories $T\to T'$: functors $T(C)\to T'(C)$ compatible with the transitions; they form a category $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(T,T')$; theories over $D$ form a 2-category.
Constructions on $T$: $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(T,\tau)$ = functors $T(C)\to C$, compatible with change of $C$ (centre of a group, abelianisation, $G^n$).
$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(T,\tau)$ is in $\mathbf{Cat}_D$: limits of type $D'$, $D''$ and the exactness properties computed termwise in each $C$.
$I$ $D$-generates $R$ if $\operatorname{Hom}_D(R,C)\to C^I$ is faithful for all $C$.
Algebraic theories: representable by $R$ with a small generating set $I$.
Monomorphism: $X\times_YX\to X$ an isomorphism; epimorphism likewise; equality of two arrows via kernel or cokernel.
Not expressible: “$X$ acts faithfully on $Y$” (not stable under base change); “locally constant with $n$ sheets” (not representable).
Rule 3 (adding arrows): $H$ a small set with $H\to\operatorname{Fl}$ data of constructions.
